items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: INTERVIEWEE: Nick LaRocco. ... INTERVIEWER: Oh, Nick LaRocco. Was in that. Yeah.

ctx.x: Deacon Lawyer, Ken, made a classical remark. He always tells you about the old days. You know that, Raymond? I mean, I'm on a job. He always tells you about the old days. I'm on a job. No, yeah, when they call a Deacon. Yeah, he was up there. And we were talking about Tom. He was saying about, in the early days, people before Tom Brown went to Chicago, you know? And somebody in the group, or maybe it was myself, said, well, according to the records, you know, Tom Brown was the first one who took a white band to…

That's not my story. No, no. Tom Brown went up and he came back. Then that's where Nick went up. Nick and Eddie Nunez. Yeah, but the Yellow Nunez went up before Nick. And Yellow. Yellow went with Nick.

No. Yellow was recorded without Nick. Yellow was recorded with the band of this planet. He was in Louisiana 5. I said Yellow. He was in Louisiana 5. And then Nick came after them. They had a man up there before the rocker, Johnny.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: I had me and Pop Peet and tree trumpets and all of them. I had his colored doors. I forgot his name, Italian fellas playing baritone.

ctx.x: And he had hot bands. Yeah. Which you'd call a jazz band.

Yeah, called ragtime bands. Well we used to play funerals and everything. Funerals. Over in Gretham. Yeah, funerals. Yeah. I had me and Pop Peet and tree trumpets and all of them. I had his colored doors. I forgot his name, Italian fellas playing baritone. Playing David. Billy Scott, Dan Hughes playing the car. They were all broadfinding in those days until now. Yeah, Dan Hughes. That got to be real stiff and sopractic. Oh, that was after. That was after, huh? That was after, huh, Dan Hughes? Dan Hughes, yeah,…
What kind of band did you use to play? I mean, how many bands did you use?
